title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يشارك في مؤتمر الوحدة الوطنية والعيش المشترك المنعقد بالدوحة
title_en: The Sheikh Takes Part in the Conference on National Unity and Coexistence Held in Doha
body_ar: يشارك فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي اليوم وغدا الموافق 02-03 ابريل 2014مـ بإذن الله تعالى في مؤتمر تنظمه وزارة الأوقاف القطرية حول موضوع: " الوحدة الوطنية والعيش المشترك " تحتضنه العاصمة الدوحة؛ و تتمثل مشاركة فضيلة الشيخ في الجلسة الثانية من مساء يوم الاربعاء 02 ابريل 2014 بورقة بعنوان: الحريات الدينية وتطبيقاتها في نظم القضاء والوقف . ولعدم انسجام العنوان لم يتحدث الشيخ في بداية مداخلته عن الوقف فلا علاقة للوقف بموضوع الحريات الدينية و في رده على تعقيب بعض المشاركين بشأن الوقف قال الشيخ بأن " الاوقاف كبيت المال لم تكن تميز في رعايا الدولة ومواطنيها بين مسلم و غير مسلم و ذلك من العهد النبوي، فالرسول صلى الله عليه قال: "في كل ذي كبد حراء أجر" وبين ذلك في الصدقات ، وقد وقفت أم المؤمنين صفية بنت حيي بن أخطب بيتا على أخ لها يهودي مع أن الوقف كما قال الامام النووي عن الامام الشافعي مختص بالمسلمين في أصله فلم يكن في الأمم السابقة وقف؛ وبما أن الوقف يقوم على أساس طلب الأجر و الأجر في المسلمين و غيرهم كما بين ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد قامت الأوقاف الاسلامية برعاية أبناء السبيل و العناية بهم و كان التعليم يشمل المسلمين و غير هم و في الزكاة خص الله قسما منها لغير المسلمين و هو قسم المؤلفة قلوبهم و هو أحد اصناف الزكاة الثمانية التي عينها الله تعالى في كتابه فقضية الصرف المالي على مواطني الدولة من غير المسلمين لا يختص بالأوقاف فقط فهي موجودة في مختلف مصادر التمويل في الدولة الإسلامية و يشارك في هذا المؤتمر كوكبة من علماء الأمة ومفكريها إضافة إلى بعض رجال السياسة والإعلام من العالم الإسلامي والغربي
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti is taking part today and tomorrow, 02–03 April 2014, God the Exalted willing, in a conference organised by the Qatari Ministry of Endowments on the subject 'National Unity and Coexistence', hosted by the capital, Doha.

The Sheikh's contribution is a paper in the second session on the evening of Wednesday 02 April 2014, entitled 'Religious Freedoms and Their Applications in the Systems of the Judiciary and of Endowment'.

Because the title was not coherent, the Sheikh did not speak at the start of his intervention about endowment (waqf), since endowment has no connection with the subject of religious freedoms. Replying to a comment by some of the participants regarding endowment, the Sheikh said:

"Endowments, like the public treasury, did not distinguish among the state's subjects and citizens between Muslim and non-Muslim, and that from the prophetic era. The Messenger (peace be upon him) said: 'In every creature with a thirsting liver there is reward', and he made that plain in the matter of charitable giving. The Mother of the Believers, Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, endowed a house upon a Jewish brother of hers — even though endowment, as Imam al-Nawawi said on the authority of Imam al-Shafi'i, is in its origin particular to the Muslims, there having been no endowment among the earlier communities. And since endowment rests on the seeking of reward, and reward is to be had in respect of Muslims and others alike, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) made plain — and Islamic endowments have looked after wayfarers and cared for them, and education used to take in Muslims and others; and in zakat God set apart a portion for non-Muslims, namely the portion of those whose hearts are to be reconciled, which is one of the eight categories of zakat that God the Exalted designated in His Book — the question of spending public money on the state's non-Muslim citizens is not particular to endowments alone: it is present in the various sources of funding in the Islamic state."

Taking part in this conference is a company of the community's scholars and thinkers, in addition to some figures from politics and the media in the Islamic and the Western world.

flags.arabic: في كل ذي كبد حراء أجر
flags.context: the prophetic report the Sheikh cites for reward in benefiting any living creature
options: 'in every creature with a thirsting liver there is reward' (reading حرّاء, parched)
'in every moist liver there is reward' (the widely transmitted wording, كبد رطبة)
the wording is corrupt in the source
flags.note: The report is usually transmitted as في كل كبد رطبة أجر. The wording here, ذي كبد حراء, is a recognised variant sense — a creature whose liver is parched, that is, a thirsty living thing — and is what the source has. Translated on the source's wording rather than replaced with the familiar version, per house rule 11. The Sheikh gives no collection or grading, and none has been added.

flags.arabic: صفية بنت حيي بن أخطب … وقفت بيتا على أخ لها يهودي
flags.context: the precedent cited for endowing property upon a non-Muslim
options: reproduce the report as he gives it
seek the source for the report
flags.note: The Sheikh gives no chain or source for this report about Safiyyah. It is the load-bearing precedent in his argument, so a reviewer should identify it before the passage is quoted as evidence. Nothing has been supplied.

flags.arabic: قسم المؤلفة قلوبهم … خص الله قسما منها لغير المسلمين
flags.context: the argument from the categories entitled to zakat
options: record the statement as he makes it
note that the classical category is not confined to non-Muslims
flags.note: The Sheikh states that God set apart a portion of zakat for non-Muslims, identifying it as المؤلفة قلوبهم. The jurists generally treat that category as including both non-Muslims whose hearts are to be won and Muslims new to the faith, so the statement as given is narrower than the usual account. Recorded exactly as he says it, without correction or expansion.

flags.context: ولعدم انسجام العنوان لم يتحدث الشيخ في بداية مداخلته عن الوقف
options: because the title was not coherent
because the title did not hang together
because the two halves of the title did not belong together
flags.note: The site's own editorial remark, not the Sheikh's. It reports that he declined at first to address the endowment half of an assigned title he judged ill-matched. Kept, since removing it would leave the following paragraph without its occasion.

translator_notes: The quoted passage is the Sheikh's own words as the site reports them, and is the substance of the record. It is a connected argument, not a summary, and has been translated in full rather than condensed.

The Arabic runs the quoted passage as a single sentence with the conclusion suspended over three intervening clauses. The English keeps it as one sentence, set off by dashes, rather than breaking the argument into separate assertions.
صلى الله عليه appears once without وسلم in the source; translated as it stands.
The record also carries scattered missing hamzas (ابريل, الاوقاف, الاربعاء, اصناف) and a split word (غير هم); these are not individually flagged.
